knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Modulus Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp open threshold obtained from secant slopes of the value function at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\lambda_*:=\sup_{t>0}\frac{[v(0)-v(t)]_+}{t}.\] This is the least \(L\in[0,+\infty]\) satisfying \(v(t)\ge v(0)-Lt\) for all \(t\ge0\). If \(\lambda_*<+\infty\), every \(\rho>\lambda_*\) is value-exact and excludes infeasible penalized minimizers. Every \(0\le\rho<\lambda_*\) fails value exactness. Exactness at \(\rho=\lambda_*\) requires a separate equality analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest decrease in perturbation value per unit violation is the sharp open exactness threshold; behavior at the endpoint must be checked separately.
assumptions_latex: \(C:=\{x\in X:g(x)=0\}\) is nonempty, and \(v(t):=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le t\}\) satisfies \(v(0)\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\rho>\lambda_*\) is an exact penalty parameter, whereas every \(0\le\rho<\lambda_*\) fails value exactness.

notation.meaning: Least global perturbation slope governing exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local exactness threshold for the ℓ1 penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The nonsmooth exact-penalty specialization contained in a composite paragraph that also discusses smooth penalties, augmented Lagrangians, and Courant-penalty failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) solve the equality-constrained problem with Lagrange multiplier \(\lambda^*\). Set \(A^*=A(x^*)\) and \(W^*=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*)\). If \(d^TW^*d>0\) for every nonzero \(d\) satisfying \((A^*)^Td=0\), then, for \(\sigma>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\), \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer of the \(\ell_1\) penalty function; consequently, that penalty is locally exact at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an equality-constrained solution satisfying the stated second-order sufficient condition, an l1 penalty weight larger than the infinity norm of the solution multiplier makes the solution a strict local minimizer of the penalty function, establishing local exactness.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ is a strict local minimizer of the }\ell_1\text{ penalty function, which is locally exact at }x^*.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Exactness Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Localized value-function threshold around a fixed constrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), define \[v_U(t):=\inf\{f(x):x\in U,\ g(x)\le t\},\qquad \lambda_U(\bar x):=\sup_{t>0}\frac{[f(\bar x)-v_U(t)]_+}{t}.\] If \(\lambda_U(\bar x)<+\infty\), every \(\rho>\lambda_U(\bar x)\) satisfies \[f(x)+\rho g(x)\ge f(\bar x)\quad\text{for all }x\in U.\] Hence \(\bar x\) is a local penalized minimizer, and every \(x\in U\) with \(f(x)+\rho g(x)=f(\bar x)\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite localized perturbation slope is a strict local exactness threshold and excludes infeasible points attaining the local penalized minimum value.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and \(f(\bar x)=\inf\{f(x):x\in C\cap U\}\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho>\lambda_U(\bar x)\), then \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f+\rho g\), and every point in \(U\) attaining the same penalized value is feasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Exactness Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global threshold expressed directly through objective improvement divided by constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(\sup\varnothing:=0\), define \[\Lambda:=\sup_{\substack{x\in X,\ g(x)>0\\ f(x)<f_*}}\frac{f_*-f(x)}{g(x)}.\] If \(\Lambda<+\infty\), every \(\rho>\Lambda\) satisfies \[\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\rho g(x)\bigr)=f_*,\] and every attained penalized minimizer is feasible and constrained-optimal. Every \(0\le\rho<\Lambda\) fails global value exactness. The endpoint \(\rho=\Lambda\) requires separate analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst objective improvement per unit positive violation is the sharp open global exactness threshold; the endpoint requires a separate check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\Lambda<+\infty\), every \(\rho>\Lambda\) is globally exact; every \(0\le\rho<\Lambda\) fails equality of the penalized and constrained infima.

children.title: Uniform Exactness Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Penalty levels valid across a prescribed family of problems or points.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Exactness Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One penalty parameter valid across an entire prescribed family of constrained problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in P\), define \[\Lambda(p):=\sup_{\substack{x\in X,\ g_p(x)>0\\ f_p(x)<f_p^*}}\frac{f_p^*-f_p(x)}{g_p(x)},\qquad \overline\Lambda:=\sup_{p\in P}\Lambda(p),\] with \(\sup\varnothing:=0\). The family admits a finite uniform strict exactness threshold if and only if \(\overline\Lambda<+\infty\). In that case, every \(\rho>\overline\Lambda\) is exact for every \(p\in P\), and every attained penalized minimizer is feasible. If \(\overline\Lambda=+\infty\), no finite penalty weight is exact for every member of the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family has a finite uniform strict exactness threshold exactly when its pointwise global thresholds are uniformly bounded.
assumptions_latex: For each \(p\in P\), \(f_p:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(g_p:X\to[0,+\infty]\), and \(C_p:=\{x\in X:g_p(x)=0\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite \(\overline\Lambda\) is a uniform strict exactness threshold, and every \(\rho>\overline\Lambda\) is exact simultaneously for all \(p\in P\).

children.title: Parametric Exactness Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Penalty levels varying with external or reformulation parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Exactness Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise threshold selection for parameterized exact-penalty problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(p\in P\), define \[\Lambda(p):=\sup_{\substack{x\in X,\ g_p(x)>0\\ f_p(x)<f_p^*}}\frac{f_p^*-f_p(x)}{g_p(x)},\] with \(\sup\varnothing:=0\). If \(\rho(p)>\Lambda(p)\), then \[\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f_p(x)+\rho(p)g_p(x)\bigr)=f_p^*,\] and every attained penalized minimizer is feasible and constrained-optimal. If \(0\le\rho(p)<\Lambda(p)\), value exactness fails at \(p\). Exactness at equality requires a separate check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each parameter value has its own sharp open exactness threshold, permitting pointwise selection of the penalty weight.
assumptions_latex: For each \(p\in P\), \(f_p:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(g_p:X\to[0,+\infty]\), and \(C_p:=\{x\in X:g_p(x)=0\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameter-dependent penalty \(\rho(p)\) is strictly exact whenever \(\rho(p)>\Lambda(p)\); no selection with \(\rho(p)<\Lambda(p)\) is value-exact at that parameter.

children.title: Threshold Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Persistence of exactness thresholds under parameter variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Stability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper-semicontinuity regime ensuring persistence of a strict penalty margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Lambda(p_0)<+\infty\) and \(\Lambda\) is upper semicontinuous at \(p_0\), then for every \(\rho>\Lambda(p_0)\) there exists a neighborhood \(V\) of \(p_0\) such that \(\rho>\Lambda(p)\) for all \(p\in V\). Therefore the same weight \(\rho\) is an exact penalty parameter throughout \(V\), and every attained penalized minimizer there is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper semicontinuity of a finite pointwise threshold preserves every strict penalty margin on a neighborhood of the reference parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a topological space, \(p_0\in P\), and \(\Lambda:P\to[0,+\infty]\) is the pointwise global exactness-threshold function for a parameterized family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\rho>\Lambda(p_0)\) remains an exact penalty parameter for all parameters in some neighborhood of \(p_0\).

children.title: Threshold Blow-Up Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where usable threshold control becomes unbounded or unstable.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Blow-Up Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar degeneration showing threshold blow-up when violation scaling vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For this family, the open exactness threshold is \[\Lambda(p)=\frac{1}{p}.\] Thus every fixed \(p>0\) admits strictly exact penalties \(\rho>1/p\), while \(\Lambda(p)\to+\infty\) as \(p\downarrow0\). Consequently, no finite penalty parameter is uniformly exact on any parameter set containing arbitrarily small positive \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the violation scale vanishes with the parameter, the exact penalty threshold diverges and no finite uniform threshold survives near the boundary.
assumptions_latex: Strict exactness means equality of penalized and constrained optimal values together with feasibility of every attained penalized minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although every \(p>0\) admits strictly exact penalties, \(\Lambda(p)=1/p\to+\infty\) as \(p\downarrow0\), so no finite uniform threshold exists near the degeneracy boundary.

children.title: Local Minimizer Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of locally minimizing solutions between constrained plus penalized formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Minimizer Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local transfer under Lipschitz continuity and a local error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\rho\ge L\kappa\), then \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(P_\rho:=f+\rho g\). If \(\rho>L\kappa\), there exists a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\) such that every \(x\in V\) satisfying \(P_\rho(x)=P_\rho(\bar x)\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Lipschitz continuity and a local error bound transfer a constrained local minimizer to the penalty problem at weights at least their modulus product; a strict weight excludes nearby infeasible minimizers at the same value.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and closed, \(\bar x\in C\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfies \(C=\{x:g(x)=0\}\).
There is a neighborhood \(U_0\) of \(\bar x\) such that \(f(\bar x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\cap U_0\).
The function \(f\) is finite and \(L\)-Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa g(x)\) holds on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), for constants \(L,\kappa\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\rho\ge L\kappa\), \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f+\rho g\); if \(\rho>L\kappa\), nearby points attaining the same penalized value are feasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Minimizer Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional global transfer under global Lipschitz continuity and a global error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\rho\ge L\kappa\), the constrained minimizer \(x_*\) globally minimizes \(P_\rho:=f+\rho g\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). If \(\rho>L\kappa\), every global minimizer of \(P_\rho\) is feasible and globally minimizes \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global Lipschitz bound and a global error bound transfer a constrained global solution to the penalty problem at weights at least their modulus product; a strict weight excludes infeasible global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and closed, and \(x_*\in C\) satisfies \(f(x_*)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).
\(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfies \(C=\{x:g(x)=0\}\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa g(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), for some \(\kappa\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\rho\ge L\kappa\), \(x_*\) globally minimizes \(f+\rho g\); for \(\rho>L\kappa\), every global penalized minimizer is feasible and constrained-optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Converse Minimizer Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Automatic reverse transfer after feasibility of a penalized minimizer has been established.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\rho\ge0\), the restrictions of the objectives to the feasible set satisfy \(P_\rho|_C=f|_C\). Consequently, every feasible local minimizer of \(P_\rho\) on \(X\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\), and every feasible global minimizer of \(P_\rho\) on \(X\) is a global minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once a penalized minimizer is known to be feasible, it automatically solves the corresponding constrained problem because the penalty vanishes on the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The penalized minimizer under consideration belongs to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible local, respectively global, minimizer of \(P_\rho\) is a local, respectively global, minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\rho\) has no minimizer when \(\rho<1\), every \(x\ge0\) is a global minimizer when \(\rho=1\), and \(x=0\) is its unique global minimizer when \(\rho>1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar equality-constrained boundary example showing the sharp exact-penalty threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the constrained problem \(\min\{-x:x=0\}\), whose unique feasible minimizer is \(x=0\), and its penalty \(P_\rho(x)=-x+\rho|x|\). For \(x\ge0\), \(P_\rho(x)=(\rho-1)x\), while for \(x<0\), \(P_\rho(x)=-(1+\rho)x>0\). Hence \(\rho<1\) makes the penalized problem unbounded below; at \(\rho=1\), every \(x\ge0\) is a global minimizer, including infeasible points; and for \(\rho>1\), the constrained solution \(x=0\) is the unique global minimizer. Thus spurious minimizers occur at the threshold itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar equality problem has infeasible penalized minimizers exactly at the threshold; above it, only the constrained minimizer remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Spurious-Minimizer Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke-stationarity transfer for a finite-dimensional equality-residual penalty with a smooth objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\lVert h(x)\rVert_1\). At any \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(h(\bar x)=0\), \[0\in\partial_C P_\rho(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists\lambda\in[-\rho,\rho]^m:\ \nabla f(\bar x)+Dh(\bar x)^\top\lambda=0.\] Consequently, a feasible equality-constrained stationary pair \((\bar x,\lambda)\) transfers to Clarke stationarity of \(P_\rho\) whenever \(\rho\ge\lVert\lambda\rVert_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth objective and equality mapping, feasible stationarity transfers to the one-norm penalty exactly when the associated multiplier is bounded in infinity norm by the penalty weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial_C P_\rho(\bar x)\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in[-\rho,\rho]^m\) such that \(\nabla f(\bar x)+Dh(\bar x)^\top\lambda=0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative global transfer under an error bound and attained nearest-point projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\inf_{z\in C}f(z)\). For a nearest feasible point \(z\), Lipschitz continuity and the error bound imply \(f(x)\ge f(z)-L\kappa v(x)\ge f^*-L\kappa v(x)\). Therefore \(P_\rho(x)\ge f^*+(\rho-L\kappa)v(x)\). If \(P_\rho(x)\le f^*+\varepsilon\), then \(v(x)\le\varepsilon/(\rho-L\kappa)\). Moreover, \(f(z)\le f(x)+L\kappa v(x)\le f^*+\varepsilon+L\kappa\varepsilon/(\rho-L\kappa)\). Thus an approximate penalized solution yields controlled infeasibility and a quantitatively approximate feasible solution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract global exactness definition for smooth penalties obtained by lifting the variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuously differentiable family \(F_\rho:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is an auxiliary-variable smooth exact penalty for \(\min\{f(x):x\in C\}\) if there exists \(\bar\rho<\infty\) such that, for every \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\), \[\operatorname{proj}_X\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in X\times Y}F_\rho(x,y)\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x).\] Local exactness at \(\bar x\) is defined by replacing global argmin sets with local minimizers in neighborhoods of \((\bar x,\bar y)\) and \(\bar x\). Smoothness refers to the lifted variables jointly; eliminating \(y\) may recover a nonsmooth reduced penalty.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A smooth two-parameter family \(P_{\rho,\mu}\) is parametrically exact for \(\min\{f(x):x\in C\}\) if there exist finite parameters \(\bar\rho>0\) and \(\bar\mu>0\) such that \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}P_{\bar\rho,\bar\mu}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x),\] with equality interpreted locally when local exactness is intended. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), \(0\le |t|-\phi_\mu(t)\le\mu\), and \(\phi_\mu(t)\to|t|\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). Hence \[P_{\rho,\mu}(x)=f(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\sqrt{c_i(x)^2+\mu^2}-\mu\right)\] satisfies \[0\le f(x)+\rho\|c(x)\|_1-P_{\rho,\mu}(x)\le\rho m\mu.\] If \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable, then \(P_{\rho,\mu}\) is continuously differentiable for every \(\mu>0\), while its pointwise limit is the nonsmooth \(\ell_1\) penalty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional log-sum-exp smoothing of a maximum-violation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[M_\mu(x)=\mu\log\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\exp(r_i(x)/\mu)\right).\] Then, for every \(x\), \[\max_{1\le i\le m}r_i(x)\le M_\mu(x)\le\max_{1\le i\le m}r_i(x)+\mu\log m.\] Thus \(f(x)+\rho M_\mu(x)\) uniformly approximates the maximum-violation penalty \(f(x)+\rho\max_i r_i(x)\) with error at most \(\rho\mu\log m\). If all \(r_i\) and \(f\) are continuously differentiable, the smoothed penalty is continuously differentiable for every \(\mu>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A smoothing family has the sequential consistency certificate at \(\bar x\) if, for every sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) and every \(\mu_k\downarrow0\), \[\|\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k)\|\to0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\Phi_0(\bar x)=0.\] A sufficient certificate is local uniform consistency: there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and a function \(\omega:(0,\bar\mu]\to\mathbb{R}_+\) with \(\omega(\mu)\to0\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\) such that \[\sup_{x\in U}\|\Phi_\mu(x)-\Phi_0(x)\|\leq\omega(\mu)\qquad(0<\mu\leq\bar\mu).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The solution \(\bar x\) is pointwise regular for the complementarity residual \(\Phi\) if \[\det V\neq0\qquad\text{for every }V\in\partial\Phi(\bar x).\] Because \(\partial\Phi(\bar x)\) is compact, this is equivalently the existence of \(M<\infty\) such that \[\sup_{V\in\partial\Phi(\bar x)}\|V^{-1}\|\leq M.\] The condition concerns only generalized derivatives at \(\bar x\); it does not by itself assert nonsingularity of smoothing Jacobians at nearby points and positive smoothing parameters. If \(\sup_k\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\) is sufficiently small, then the inexact iteration retains local linear convergence. If \(\eta_k\to0\) and the smoothing and semismoothness errors are \(o(\|x_k-\bar x\|)\), then \[\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|=o(\|x_k-bar x\|).\] Quadratic convergence is retained when \(\eta_k=O(\|x_k-bar x\|)\) and all other local errors are of quadratic order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Controlled linear-solve errors preserve convergence: bounded small forcing gives a linear rate, vanishing forcing gives superlinear convergence, and first-order forcing can retain quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Convergence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits, but the superlinear and quadratic formulas contain \(x_k-bar x\) instead of \(x_k-\bar x\), and no source supports the exact forcing-term thresholds or their interaction with smoothing errors. The mathematical version therefore requires a source before revision.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A vector solves the nonlinear complementarity problem exactly when it is nonnegative, its image is nonnegative, and their inner product is zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional nonlinear complementarity problem.

source_refs.locator: 9.1 Nonlinear Complementarity Problems p. 794
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nonlinear complementarity problem associated with \(F\), denoted \(\operatorname{NCP}(F)\), is to find \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \[x\geq0,\qquad F(x)\geq0,\qquad x^{\mathsf T}F(x)=0.\] The inequalities are componentwise. Equivalently, \(x_iF_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), written \(0\leq x\perp F(x)\geq0\). For any scalar complementarity function \(\phi\) satisfying \(\phi(a,b)=0\) exactly when \(a\geq0\), \(b\geq0\), and \(ab=0\), the problem is equivalently the nonsmooth equation \(\Phi(x)=0\), where \(\Phi_i(x)=\phi(x_i,F_i(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An NCP seeks a nonnegative vector whose nonlinear image is nonnegative and componentwise complementary to it; complementarity functions convert the conditions into residual equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Complementarity Problems

source_witnesses.locator: 9.1 Nonlinear Complementarity Problems p. 794
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

assumptions_latex: The bounds satisfy \(-\infty\leq l_i<u_i\leq+\infty\) for every component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mixed-complementarity solution satisfies a sign condition determined by whether each component is at its lower bound, in the interior, or at its upper bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional mixed complementarity problem with possibly infinite bounds.

source_refs.locator: 9.4.2 Mixed complementarity problems p. 866
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mixed complementarity problem \(\operatorname{MCP}(F,l,u)\) is to find \(x\in[l,u]\) such that, for each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \[\begin{cases}F_i(x)\geq0,&x_i=l_i,\\F_i(x)=0,&l_i<x_i<u_i,\\F_i(x)\leq0,&x_i=u_i.\end{cases}\] At a component fixed by \(l_i=u_i\), no sign restriction is imposed; such components are excluded here by the strict bound assumption. Equivalently, the displayed alternatives state \(0\in F(x)+N_{[l,u]}(x)\), where \(N_{[l,u]}(x)\) is the convex-analytic normal cone. The nonlinear complementarity problem is recovered by taking \(l=0\) and \(u=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An MCP imposes nonnegative residuals at lower bounds, zero residuals in the interior, and nonpositive residuals at upper bounds, component by component.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Complementarity Problems

source_witnesses.locator: 9.4.2 Mixed complementarity problems p. 866
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

assumptions_latex: The box \(K=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The box variational inequality is equivalent to the mixed complementarity sign alternatives and to the normal-cone inclusion \(0\in F(x)+N_K(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional variational inequality over a box and its complementarity representation.

source_refs.locator: 9.4.2 Mixed complementarity problems p. 866
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The box-constrained variational inequality is to find \(x\in K\) such that \[\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }y\in K.\] This condition is equivalent to \[0\in F(x)+N_K(x).\] Because \(K\) is a Cartesian product of intervals, the inclusion is equivalent componentwise to \[F_i(x)\geq0\ \text{if }x_i=l_i,\qquad F_i(x)=0\ \text{if }l_i<x_i<u_i,\qquad F_i(x)\leq0\ \text{if }x_i=u_i.\] Hence a box-constrained variational inequality and the associated mixed complementarity problem have exactly the same solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variational inequality over a box is exactly a mixed complementarity problem, equivalently a normal-cone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constrained Variational Inequalities

assumptions_latex: For each \(x\in\mathbb{R}^p\), the equilibrium feasible set \(K(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An equilibrium-constrained program minimizes \(f(x,y)\) subject to \(g(x,y)\leq0\) and the requirement that \(y\) solve a parameterized variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical program constrained by a parameterized variational equilibrium.

source_refs.locator: 5.2.2 Variational Systems as Equilibrium Constraints p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An equilibrium-constrained program has the form \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^p,\,y\in\mathbb{R}^q} f(x,y)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g(x,y)\leq0,\quad y\in S(x),\] where the inequality is componentwise and the equilibrium solution map is \[S(x)=\left\{y\in K(x):\langle F(x,y),z-y\rangle\geq0\ \text{for every }z\in K(x)\right\}.\] Equivalently, the equilibrium constraint is the generalized equation \[0\in F(x,y)+N_{K(x)}(y).\] When \(K(x)\) is a box, the lower-level condition can be represented as a mixed complementarity system and then by complementarity-function equations or smooth approximations. The equilibrium condition is part of the feasible-set definition rather than an independently optimized lower-level objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equilibrium-constrained program optimizes an upper-level objective while requiring its equilibrium variable to solve a parameterized variational inequality or equivalent generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Equilibrium-Constrained Programs

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Complementarity Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise nonlinear complementarity at a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(x^*\) solve \(0\le x\perp F(x)\ge0\). Define \(I_0=\{i:x_i^*=0,\ F_i(x^*)=0\}\). The complementarity point \(x^*\) is degenerate when \(I_0\ne\varnothing\); equivalently, strict complementarity fails in at least one component. It is nondegenerate in the complementarity sense when, for every \(i\), exactly one of \(x_i^*\) and \(F_i(x^*)\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complementarity solution is degenerate when some component has both the primal variable and its complementary residual equal to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\text{ is degenerate}\iff \{i:x_i^*=F_i(x^*)=0\}\ne\varnothing\)

notation.meaning: set of biactive or doubly zero complementarity indices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complementarity-degeneracy definition is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but no inspectable authoritative locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Smoothed Jacobians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-loss condition for a square smoothed residual system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\bar\mu]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable in \(x\), and suppose \(H(x,\mu)=0\). The smoothed state Jacobian is singular at \((x,\mu)\) precisely when \(D_xH(x,\mu)\) is not invertible, equivalently when \(\det D_xH(x,\mu)=0\) or \(\operatorname{rank}D_xH(x,\mu)<n\). At such a point, the standard implicit-function theorem does not guarantee a local differentiable representation \(x=x(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smoothed state Jacobian is singular when it loses full rank; then the standard implicit-function theorem no longer guarantees a locally differentiable parameterization by the smoothing parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_xH(x,\mu)\text{ is singular}\iff \operatorname{rank}D_xH(x,\mu)<n\)

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the smoothed residual with respect to the decision variable

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Complementarity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of monotonicity for a complementarity residual map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), a nonmonotone complementarity regime is present on \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) when there exist \(x,y\in D\) such that \(\langle F(x)-F(y),x-y\rangle<0\). For example, \(F(x)=-x\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) satisfies \((F(x)-F(y))(x-y)=-(x-y)^2<0\) whenever \(x\ne y\). Consequently, convergence arguments requiring monotonicity of the complementarity mapping do not apply on that regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regime is nonmonotone when two points violate the monotonicity inequality; the scalar map F(x)=-x is a concrete example.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x,y\in D:\langle F(x)-F(y),x-y\rangle<0\)
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the complementarity-specific failure boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity violation and scalar counterexample are correct, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. A complementarity-specific source is absent, and the statement alternates between F defined on all of Euclidean space and on D.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Merit-Function Level Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of level-boundedness for a complementarity merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Psi:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a merit function. Its sublevel set at \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\) is \(L_\alpha=\{x:\Psi(x)\le\alpha\}\). The merit function has an unbounded level set when \(L_\alpha\) is unbounded for some finite \(\alpha\); equivalently, there is a sequence \(x^k\) with \(\|x^k\|\to\infty\) and \(\Psi(x^k)\le\alpha\). Hence descent confined to that sublevel set alone does not guarantee bounded iterates or accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit-function sublevel set is unbounded when points can escape to infinity while their merit values remain below one finite threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_\alpha\text{ unbounded}\iff \exists x^k:\|x^k\|\to\infty,\ \Psi(x^k)\le\alpha\)

notation.meaning: sublevel set of the merit function at level alpha

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing Homotopy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuation through stationary points of smooth approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given smooth functions \(f_\mu:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(\mu>0\), choose \(\mu_0>\mu_1>\cdots\downarrow0\), an initial point \(x^0\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), approximately solve the smooth subproblem at \(\mu_k\), warm-starting from \(x^{k-1}\), until \(\|\nabla f_{\mu_k}(x^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k\). Stop at a prescribed terminal parameter or accuracy and return the last iterate. Cluster points are candidate stationary points of the limiting nonsmooth problem only under an appropriate gradient-consistency assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve successively less-smoothed problems, warm-start each from the preceding solution, and reduce both the smoothing parameter and stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f_{\mu_k}(x^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k\) at every completed stage

notation.meaning: smoothing parameter at continuation stage k
smooth stationarity tolerance at stage k

review_flags: No supplied locator identifies a smoothing-homotopy algorithm or its gradient-consistency hypotheses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic smoothing-continuation scheme requires a supporting locator, particularly for gradient consistency. Its stage-zero warm start also refers to the undefined iterate x^{-1}.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Continuation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuation by increasing an exterior-penalty weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constrained problem \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), choose \(0<\rho_0<\rho_1<\cdots\uparrow\infty\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), and \(x^0\). At stage \(k\), approximately minimize \(P_{\rho_k}(x)=f(x)+\rho_k\|c(x)\|^2/2\), initialized at \(x^{k-1}\), until \(\|\nabla P_{\rho_k}(x^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k\). Increase \(\rho_k\) until the requested feasibility and stationarity tests hold, then return \(x^k\). Constrained-stationarity conclusions require bounded iterates and a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize penalized objectives while increasing the penalty weight, using each stage as the next warm start, until feasibility and stationarity tests pass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla P_{\rho_k}(x^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k\) at every completed stage

notation.meaning: penalty weight at continuation stage k

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this exterior-penalty continuation version.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this particular quadratic exterior-penalty continuation algorithm. The stage-zero warm start uses x^{-1}, and the codomain of the constraint map c is not introduced.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-Parameter Continuation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuation through Moreau-envelope stationary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For \(\lambda>0\), define \(e_\lambda f(x)=\inf_y\{f(y)+\|y-x\|^2/(2\lambda)\}\). Choose \(\lambda_k>0\) with \(\lambda_k\downarrow0\), an initial \(x^0\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\). At stage \(k\), warm-start from \(x^{k-1}\) and find \(x^k\) satisfying \(\|\nabla e_{\lambda_k}f(x^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k\). Stop at the prescribed terminal parameter or accuracy and return the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track approximate stationary points of Moreau envelopes while reducing the envelope parameter toward zero, warm-starting every stage.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla e_{\lambda_k}f(x^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k\) at every completed stage

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope of f with parameter lambda

review_flags: No supplied locator supports the chosen convex Moreau-envelope continuation version.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex Moreau-envelope formula is standard, but the proposed continuation algorithm has no locator and refers to x^{-1} at its initial stage.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Smoothing Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer–Burmeister smoothing path for nonlinear complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and define \(\phi_\mu(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+2\mu^2}-a-b\) for \(\mu>0\). With \(\Phi_\mu(x)_i=\phi_\mu(x_i,F_i(x))\), the smoothed complementarity path is \(S(\mu)=\{x:\Phi_\mu(x)=0\}\). Each path point satisfies \(x_i>0\), \(F_i(x)>0\), and \(x_iF_i(x)=\mu^2\) for every \(i\). If \(\mu_k\downarrow0\), \(x^k\in S(\mu_k)\), and \(x^k\to x^*\), then \(0\le x^*\perp F(x^*)\ge0\), provided \(F\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smoothed Fischer–Burmeister zeros satisfy positive perturbed complementarity products; every finite limit as smoothing vanishes solves the original complementarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in S(\mu)\iff x_i>0,\ F_i(x)>0,\ x_iF_i(x)=\mu^2\ \text{for all }i\)

notation.meaning: solution set of the smoothed complementarity system

review_flags: Exact smoothing formula is standard but no complementarity-smoothing locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated smoothing equation correctly yields positive components with product μ², and continuity gives the asserted complementarity limit. An authoritative complementarity-smoothing locator is nevertheless required for this formula and representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Smooth Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local implicit-function characterization of a continuation branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable near \((\bar x,\bar t)\), suppose \(H(\bar x,\bar t)=0\), and assume \(D_xH(\bar x,\bar t)\) is nonsingular. Then neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar t\) and \(V\) of \(\bar x\) contain a unique continuously differentiable path \(x:U\to V\) satisfying \(x(\bar t)=\bar x\) and \(H(x(t),t)=0\). Its tangent obeys \(x'(t)=-D_xH(x(t),t)^{-1}D_tH(x(t),t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular state Jacobian makes the nearby solution set a unique smooth path, whose tangent follows the differentiated continuation equation.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is continuously differentiable near \((\bar x,\bar t)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists!\,x\in C^1(U;V):H(x(t),t)=0,\quad x'(t)=-D_xH(x(t),t)^{-1}D_tH(x(t),t)\)

notation.meaning: Jacobian with respect to the state variable

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Solution Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution mapping induced by a parameterized generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a parameter set, let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional space, and let \(G:T\times X\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) be a set-valued mapping. The associated set-valued solution path is \(S:T\rightrightarrows X\) defined by \(S(t)=\{x\in X:0\in G(t,x)\}\). It has multiple solutions at \(t\) when \(|S(t)|>1\), and it is empty at \(t\) when no \(x\in X\) satisfies the generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued solution path assigns to each continuation parameter the set of all states solving the corresponding generalized equation.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Smooth Active-Set Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite active-set decomposition of a continuous continuation trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be a continuous continuation trajectory, and let \(a=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=b\). Suppose that on each interval \((t_{j-1},t_j)\) the active set is constant and the trajectory satisfies a reduced system \(R_j(x(t),t)=0\), where \(R_j:\mathbb{R}^n\times(t_{j-1},t_j)\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable and \(D_xR_j(x(t),t)\) is nonsingular for every \(t\in(t_{j-1},t_j)\). Then \(x\in C^1((t_{j-1},t_j);\mathbb{R}^n)\) for every \(j\). Thus failure of differentiability can occur only at the switching parameters \(t_1,\ldots,t_{N-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous active-set trajectory is smooth between finitely many switches when each fixed-active-set reduced system is continuously differentiable and has a nonsingular state Jacobian along the trajectory.
assumptions_latex: \(a=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=b\) and the active set is constant on each \((t_{j-1},t_j)\)
\(R_j(x(t),t)=0\) and \(D_xR_j(x(t),t)\) is nonsingular on each open interval
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in C^1((t_{j-1},t_j);\mathbb{R}^n)\text{ for every }j\)

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Continuation Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter singularity and regular-level-set failure in continuation systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(\mathcal S=\{(x,t):H(x,t)=0\}\). A continuation point \((\bar x,\bar t)\in\mathcal S\) is singular with respect to the distinguished parameter \(t\) when \(D_xH(\bar x,\bar t)\) is singular. The defining equation fails the regular-level-set condition there when \(\operatorname{rank}D_{(x,t)}H(\bar x,\bar t)<n\). State-Jacobian singularity removes the ordinary implicit-function guarantee of a representation \(x=x(t)\). If instead \(D_{(x,t)}H(\bar x,\bar t)\) has rank \(n\), the zero set is locally a one-dimensional continuously differentiable manifold even though \(D_xH(\bar x,\bar t)\) may be singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuation point is parameter-singular when the state Jacobian loses rank. Rank of the full derivative separately determines whether the regular-level-set theorem describes the nearby zero set as a smooth curve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_xH(\bar x,\bar t)\text{ singular}\); the regular-level-set condition fails if \(\operatorname{rank}D_{(x,t)}H(\bar x,\bar t)<n\)

notation.meaning: zero set of the continuation system

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The continuation path bifurcates at \((z_*,\tau_*)\) exactly when every neighborhood of that point contains solutions belonging to at least two locally distinct connected branches.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z=\{(z,\tau):F(z,\tau)=0\}\). A solution \((z_*,\tau_*)\in\mathcal Z\) is a bifurcation point if, for every neighborhood \(U\) of \((z_*,\tau_*)\), the punctured set \((\mathcal Z\cap U)\setminus\{(z_*,\tau_*)\}\) contains points from at least two connected local solution branches whose germs at \((z_*,\tau_*)\) are distinct. Consequently, no single-valued local graph \(z=z(\tau)\) represents all nearby solutions. Singularity of \(D_zF(z_*,\tau_*)\) is necessary for such failure of the implicit-function representation, but it is not by itself sufficient for bifurcation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuation solution bifurcates when every neighborhood contains at least two distinct local solution branches; a singular state Jacobian is necessary but not sufficient.

Let \(F(z(s),	au(s))=0\) and suppose \((z'(s_*),	au'(s_*))

children.title: Branch-Selection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ambiguous or unstable selection among nearby continuation branches.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Z=\{(z,	au):F(z,	au)=0\}\) has finitely many local branch germs at \((z_*,	au_*)\).
A branch-selection rule is represented by a continuous score \(q\) on each regular branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The branch-selection boundary is the subset where two or more admissible branch scores tie for the selected value, so the selected branch is not locally unique.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-based boundary for selecting among locally admissible continuation branches.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) be the admissible local branch germs of \(\mathcal Z\), and let the rule select a point on a branch minimizing a continuous score \(q\). The branch-selection boundary is the set of continuation states and parameters at which \(q(B_i)=q(B_j)=\min_{1\le k\le m}q(B_k)\) for some \(i\ne j\). Off this boundary, a strict score gap makes the selected branch locally unique. On the boundary, arbitrarily small perturbations of data, initialization, or parameters may change the selected branch even when every individual branch remains regular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branch-selection boundary is where two admissible continuation branches tie under the selection score, destroying local uniqueness and allowing small perturbations to switch branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Prescribed Parameter Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic stage schedule fixed independently of all computed information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a predetermined sequence \((\theta_k)_{k\ge0}\) with \(\theta_k\to\theta_*\), an initial point \(x_{-1}\), stage tolerances \((\varepsilon_k)_{k\ge0}\), and a stopping index or test. At stage \(k\), run the inner solver on \(P_{\theta_k}\), initialized at \(x_{k-1}\), until its prescribed error measure is at most \(\varepsilon_k\); denote the result by \(x_k\). Advance to \(\theta_{k+1}\) without using computed residuals or iterates to alter the sequence. Return \(x_k\) when the stopping rule holds. If infinitely many stages are specified, accumulation points may be considered only when they exist; their existence or convergence requires separate assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prescribed schedule fixes all continuation parameters in advance, solves each stage to its assigned tolerance, and never modifies future parameters using computed information. Infinite-stage convergence requires separate assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta_0,\theta_1,\ldots\in\Theta\) is fixed before the iteration and has target limit \(\theta_*\in\overline{\Theta}\).
For each \(\theta_k\), an inner solver accepts an initial point and returns an approximate solution of \(P_{\theta_k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The schedule is prescribed because every \(\theta_k\) is independent of computed iterates and residuals. It returns a stage iterate when its stopping rule holds; no accumulation-point or convergence guarantee follows without additional assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictor–Corrector Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent prediction followed by residual correction on a regular solution path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a corrected point \((z_k,\tau_k)\), solve \(D_zF(z_k,\tau_k)t_k=-D_\tau F(z_k,\tau_k)\) for the path tangent. Choose \(\tau_{k+1}=\tau_k+\Delta\tau_k\) and form the predictor \(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm p}=z_k+\Delta\tau_k t_k\). Starting from \(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm p}\), apply the corrector at fixed \(\tau_{k+1}\) until the prescribed residual or correction tolerance holds; call the result \(z_{k+1}\). Repeat until the outer stopping rule holds. Near singular state Jacobians, replace parameter prediction by a regular parametrization or reject the step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a tangent-based prediction at the next parameter, correct it back to the solution equation, and reject or reparametrize steps near singular Jacobians.
assumptions_latex: \(F(z,\tau)=0\) defines a regular local solution path where \(D_zF\) is nonsingular.
A parameter increment \(\Delta\tau_k\), corrector, and correction tolerance are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Predictor–corrector tracking first predicts by the path tangent and then corrects the prediction onto the residual equation at the new parameter.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-inner continuation with explicitly controlled nonzero stage errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(x_{-1}\), parameter values \((\theta_k)\), residuals \((r_k)\), tolerances \((\varepsilon_k)\), an inner solver, and an outer stopping rule. At stage \(k\), initialize at \(x_{k-1}\), apply inner iterations until an iterate \(x_k\) satisfies \(r_k(x_k)\le\varepsilon_k\), and then advance to \(\theta_{k+1}\). Return the last iterate when the outer rule holds. The stage errors are explicit algorithmic data; convergence to a target solution requires a separate compatibility condition relating \((\varepsilon_k)\), parameter changes, and stability of the stage solution mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Advance after each stage residual falls below its assigned nonzero tolerance; convergence additionally requires tolerances and parameter changes compatible with solution-map stability.

A tolerance sequence \((\varepsilon_k)\) and parameter sequence \((\theta_k)\) are given.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}F_{\theta_0}\), choose schedules \((\mu_k)\), \((\rho_k)\), and \((\varepsilon_k)\). At iteration \(k\), perform one finite inner update, initialized at \(x_k\), that returns \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname{dom}F_{\theta_k}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F_{\theta_k}(x_{k+1}))\leq\varepsilon_k\). Then update the parameters to \(\theta_{k+1}=(\mu_{k+1},\rho_{k+1})\). Stop when prescribed terminal bounds on \(\mu_k\), \(1/\rho_k\), and \(\varepsilon_k\) hold; otherwise output any cluster point of \((x_k)\), provided subsequent compatibility and boundedness conditions guarantee its validity.

assumptions_latex: The target objective \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and every \(F_\theta\) are proper and lower semicontinuous.

exact penalty and smoothing hypotheses remain model-dependent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraphical compatibility for finite-dimensional approximate global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Parameter-limit compatibility holds when \(F_{\theta_k}\xrightarrow{e}F\): for every \(x_k\to x\), \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}F_{\theta_k}(x_k)\geq F(x)\), and for every \(x\) there exists \(y_k\to x\) with \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}F_{\theta_k}(y_k)\leq F(x)\). Consequently, if \(F_{\theta_k}(x_k)\leq\inf F_{\theta_k}+\varepsilon_k\) and \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), then every cluster point of \((x_k)\) minimizes \(F\), while \(\inf F_{\theta_k}\to\inf F\) under eventual equi-level-boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parameterized objectives must converge epigraphically to the target; with uniform level control, vanishing-error stage minimizers then recover target minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Limit Compatibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Problem-independent form of the excessive-gap growth condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cancellation of problem-dependent operator and prox-diameter factors under a symmetric smoothing parametrization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume $L_1(f_{\mu_2})=\|A\|_{1,2}^2/\mu_2$. Let $D_1,D_2,\|A\|_{1,2},\lambda_1,\lambda_2>0$ and define $\mu_1=\lambda_1\|A\|_{1,2}\sqrt{D_2/D_1}$ and $\mu_2=\lambda_2\|A\|_{1,2}\sqrt{D_1/D_2}$. Then, for every $\tau\in(0,1)$, $\frac{\tau^2}{1-\tau}\leq\frac{\mu_1\mu_2}{\|A\|_{1,2}^2}$ if and only if $\frac{\tau^2}{1-\tau}\leq\lambda_1\lambda_2$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the specified Lipschitz relation and symmetric parameterization, the excessive-gap growth condition is equivalent to a problem-independent inequality involving only the update fraction and the two dimensionless scaling parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\tau^2}{1-\tau}\leq\frac{\mu_1\mu_2}{\|A\|_{1,2}^2}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\frac{\tau^2}{1-\tau}\leq\lambda_1\lambda_2.

children.title: Stage-Accuracy Requirements
children.top_down_role: Accuracy regimes imposed on successive continuation subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The returned iterate satisfies \(0\leq F_{\theta_k}(x_k)-v_k\leq\varepsilon_k\), where \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), then \(F_{\theta_k}(x_k)-v_k\to0\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value of continuation stage k.

review_flags: Objective-gap accuracy is one standard version; stationary-point continuation requires a different residual condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global stage accuracy measured by objective suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The stage-accuracy requirement is that every returned \(x_k\in\operatorname{dom}F_{\theta_k}\) obeys \(0\leq F_{\theta_k}(x_k)-v_k\leq\varepsilon_k\), where \(v_k=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}F_{\theta_k}(x)\), \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), and \(\varepsilon_k\to0\). Consequently, \(F_{\theta_k}(x_k)-v_k\to0\). If a computable lower bound \(\ell_k\leq v_k\) is used, the stronger verifiable requirement \(F_{\theta_k}(x_k)-\ell_k\leq\varepsilon_k\) suffices. This condition concerns approximate global minimization; replacing the objective gap by \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F_{\theta_k}(x_k))\) yields only a stationarity requirement unless additional error-bound assumptions are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every stage the returned objective value must lie within a nonnegative tolerance of that stage's infimum, and that tolerance must vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Stage-Accuracy Requirements

children.title: Parameter-Coupling Requirements
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between continuation parameters across successive stages.

assumptions_latex: The smoothing and penalty parameters satisfy \(\mu_k>0\) and \(\rho_k>0\).
A nonnegative approximation-bias bound \(b(\mu,\rho)\) is valid on every bounded set relevant to the iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_k\to0\), \(\rho_k\to\infty\), and \(b(\mu_k,\rho_k)\to0\).

notation.meaning: Combined smoothing and penalty bias bound.

review_flags: The form of the bias bound depends on the smoothing and penalty constructions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint asymptotic schedule expressed through a model-dependent bias bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parameter schedule is admissible when \(\mu_k\to0\), \(\rho_k\to\infty\), and its combined approximation bias vanishes: \(b(\mu_k,\rho_k)\to0\). Here \(b(\mu,\rho)\geq0\) must bound, on each relevant bounded set, the discrepancy attributable to smoothing and finite penalization. For the common separable estimate \(b(\mu,\rho)=c_s\mu+c_p/\rho\), with constants \(c_s,c_p\geq0\), the requirements reduce to \(\mu_k\to0\) and \(1/\rho_k\to0\); no fixed relative rate between them is needed unless another term couples \(\mu\) and \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smoothing must vanish and penalty strength must diverge along a schedule that drives the total approximation bias to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Coupling Requirements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the parameter-coupling leaf, but the discrepancy controlled by the bias bound is not formally defined and the separable estimate is construction-dependent. A source specifying the smoothing and penalty model is needed.

children.title: Accuracy–Parameter Balance
children.top_down_role: Relative scaling of stage accuracy against parameter reduction.

assumptions_latex: On relevant bounded sets, the parameterized model has nonnegative target bias at most \(b_k:=b(\theta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_k+b_k\to0\); the stronger balanced choice \(\varepsilon_k\leq Cb_k\) gives total error at most \((C+1)b_k\).
review_flags: The additive error decomposition must be verified for the particular smoothing-penalty construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive balance between stage optimization error and model bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The essential accuracy-parameter balance is \(\varepsilon_k+b_k\to0\), where \(\varepsilon_k\) is the stage optimization error and \(b_k=b(\theta_k)\) bounds the model bias. When computational work should not substantially exceed modeling accuracy, impose \(\varepsilon_k\leq Cb_k\) for some constant \(C<\infty\) and all sufficiently large \(k\). Then the combined error is bounded by \(\varepsilon_k+b_k\leq(C+1)b_k\). More generally, convergence needs both terms to vanish; asymptotic comparability is an efficiency rule, not a logical necessity for consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimization error and parameter-induced bias must both vanish; matching their orders avoids solving a biased stage much more accurately than useful.
knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy–Parameter Balance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the balance leaf and the arithmetic implication is correct, but the essential additive target-error decomposition is model-dependent and unsupported. A continuation-specific source is required.

children.title: Coupling Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Schedules where stage accuracy is incompatible with parameter progression.

assumptions_latex: Approximate stage solutions satisfy a target-error estimate \(E_k\leq\varepsilon_k+b(\theta_k)\), with both terms nonnegative.
At least one of \(\varepsilon_k\) or \(b(\theta_k)\) fails to converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The estimate does not imply \(E_k\to0\); specifically, \(\limsup_k(\varepsilon_k+b(\theta_k))>0\) whenever either term has positive limsup.
review_flags: This is an error-bound failure boundary, not a universal converse convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an additive accuracy-bias convergence certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An additive continuation certificate \(E_k\leq\varepsilon_k+b(\theta_k)\) cannot establish \(E_k\to0\) if either component remains nonvanishing. Fixed stage accuracy, such as \(\varepsilon_k\equiv\bar\varepsilon>0\), leaves a persistent optimization floor even when \(b(\theta_k)\to0\). Conversely, a stalled parameter path with \(\limsup_k b(\theta_k)>0\) leaves model bias even when \(\varepsilon_k\to0\). A schedule may also fail despite correct individual limits when its actual bias contains an uncontrolled interaction, for example \(b(\mu,\rho)=\mu+1/\rho+\rho\mu\) with \(\rho_k\mu_k\not\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence is uncertified if stage error, model bias, or an interaction term stays nonzero, even when some individual parameters have correct limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is correct, and the record properly avoids claiming a universal converse. The concrete interaction term and the applicability of the additive certificate nevertheless lack source support for this continuation setting.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a common compact set \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) contains the relevant level sets: \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:F_{\theta_k}(x)\leq\alpha\}\subset K\) for every sufficiently large \(k\). If \(F_{\theta_k}(x_k)\leq\alpha\) eventually, then \(x_k\in K\) eventually. Hence \((x_k)\) is bounded. In finite dimensions, every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence, so there exist indices \(k_j\uparrow\infty\) and \(\bar x\in K\) such that \(x_{k_j}\to\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform compact level set containing all sufficiently late iterates makes the continuation sequence bounded and therefore subsequentially convergent.

children.title: Cluster-Point Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of relevant limiting points from continuation subsequences.

assumptions_latex: The objectives satisfy \(F_{\theta_k}\xrightarrow{e}F\) and are eventually equi-level-bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x_k)\) satisfies \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\), and at least one such cluster point exists.

notation.meaning: A cluster point of the continuation iterates.

review_flags: The supplied locators do not directly identify the required epigraphical-convergence result.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of global minimizers from bounded approximate stage minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{\theta_k}\xrightarrow{e}F\), let the family be eventually equi-level-bounded, and suppose \(F_{\theta_k}(x_k)\leq\inf F_{\theta_k}+\varepsilon_k\) with \(\varepsilon_k\to0\). If \((x_k)\) is bounded, then it has a cluster point. For every subsequence \((x_{k_j})\) converging to \(\bar x\), one has \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\). Moreover, the minimum values converge as \(\inf F_{\theta_k}\to\inf F\). Thus boundedness supplies existence of cluster points, while epigraphical compatibility and vanishing stage error identify each cluster point as a target minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded approximate minimizers of equi-level-bounded, epigraphically convergent stage objectives have cluster points, and every such point minimizes the target.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direct boundedness route is uniform level-boundedness at the attained level: there exist \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), a bounded set \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(k_0\) such that \(\operatorname{lev}_{\alpha}F_{\theta_k}:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:F_{\theta_k}(x)\leq\alpha\}\subset B\) for every \(k\geq k_0\). Any continuation iterates satisfying \(F_{\theta_k}(x_k)\leq\alpha\) eventually are then bounded. If each \(F_{\theta_k}\) is lower semicontinuous, these sublevel sets are closed and hence compact in finite dimensions.

children.top_down_role: Failure of limiting recovery through unbounded continuation sequences.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_k(x_k)=\inf F_k=0\) but \(|x_k|\to\infty\); hence exact stage solution alone supplies no cluster point.
review_flags: This elementary counterexample is constructed for the node; the source only supports the level-boundedness boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of cluster points without uniform level-boundedness.

source_refs.locator: B. Level Sets and Intersections p. 42

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\geq1\), let \(F_k(x)=(x-k)^2/k^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\). Each \(F_k\) is continuous and coercive, and its unique exact minimizer is \(x_k=k\), with \(F_k(x_k)=\inf F_k=0\). Nevertheless, \(|x_k|\to\infty\), so the minimizer sequence has no cluster point in \(\mathbb{R}\). For every fixed \(x\), \(F_k(x)\to1\), but this pointwise parameter limit does not prevent the moving minimizers from escaping. Thus stagewise exactness and pointwise objective convergence cannot replace uniform level-boundedness or another compactness mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous coercive stage objectives can have exact minimizers escaping to infinity, so neither exact stage solution nor pointwise convergence guarantees recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Escape-to-Infinity Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K:=\min\{k\in\mathbb N_0:\tau_k\leq\tau_{\mathrm{tar}}\}\). Under the geometric schedule \(\tau_k=q^k\tau_0\), the number of parameter reductions required to reach the target is \[K=\left\lceil\frac{\log(\tau_0/\tau_{\mathrm{tar}})}{\log(1/q)}\right\rceil.\] Thus the outer-stage complexity is logarithmic in the parameter ratio when \(q\) is fixed independently of the target accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometric continuation schedule reaches the target parameter in a number of outer stages logarithmic in the initial-to-target parameter ratio.

notation.meaning: Cumulative inner work through stage K

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summation law for polynomial inner cost along a geometric parameter schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stages \(k=0,\ldots,K\), define total inner work by \(W_K:=\sum_{k=0}^{K}N_k\). If \(N_k\leq C\tau_k^{-p}\) and \(\tau_k=q^k\tau_0\), then \[W_K\leq C\sum_{k=0}^{K}\tau_k^{-p}=C\tau_K^{-p}\sum_{j=0}^{K}q^{pj}\leq\frac{C}{1-q^p}\tau_K^{-p}.\] Hence the final, most ill-conditioned stage determines the total order of inner work, up to the geometric-series factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When stage cost grows polynomially as the parameter shrinks geometrically, cumulative inner work has the same asymptotic order as the final-stage work.
knowledge_statements.title: Total Inner-Work Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At parameter \(\tau\), define \(\kappa(\tau):=L(\tau)/m(\tau)\). For any inner method whose iteration bound is a nondecreasing function \(\Phi(\kappa,\varepsilon)\) of condition number and requested stage accuracy, continuation requires at most \[\sum_{k=0}^{K}\Phi\bigl(\kappa(\tau_k),\varepsilon_k\bigr)\] inner iterations. Consequently, degeneration of \(m(\tau)\) or growth of \(L(\tau)\) near the limiting parameter can dominate complexity even when the number of outer stages is logarithmic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuation complexity must account for condition numbers along the entire parameter path; severe terminal-stage conditioning can dominate all inner work.

The conditioning diagnostic is \(\widehat\kappa_k:=\widehat L_k/\widehat m_k\). Persistent growth of \(\widehat\kappa_k\), or collapse of \(\widehat m_k\) toward zero, flags loss of uniform conditioning along the path.

children.title: Residual Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Residual-based indicators for continuation progress or solution quality.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\tau(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) is stationary for \(F_\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled first-order residual for a differentiable continuation subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The residual diagnostic at parameter \(\tau\) and point \(x\) is \[R_\tau(x):=\frac{\|\nabla F_\tau(x)\|}{s(\tau)},\] where the positive scale \(s(\tau)\) is fixed before comparing stages. A stage passes a residual tolerance \(\eta_k\geq0\) precisely when \(R_{\tau_k}(x_k)\leq\eta_k\). With a common scale, residual histories are comparable; with parameter-dependent scaling, both the scaled and unscaled residuals must be retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual diagnostic is the stage gradient norm divided by a declared positive scale; it vanishes exactly at a stationary point.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled gradient residual is correct for differentiable unconstrained stages, but it is a model-specific diagnostic choice and no supporting source or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied.

children.title: Gap Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Gap-based indicators for surrogate fidelity or optimality quality.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_\tau(x)=(F_\tau(x)-F_\tau^*)/b(\tau)\geq0\), with equality exactly at global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap diagnostic for continuation stages with an available optimal value or certified lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_\tau^*:=\min_x F_\tau(x)\). The normalized gap diagnostic is \[G_\tau(x):=\frac{F_\tau(x)-F_\tau^*}{b(\tau)}.\] It is nonnegative and equals zero exactly when \(x\) is a global minimizer. If only a certified lower bound \(\ell_\tau\leq F_\tau^*\) is available, the computable quantity \((F_\tau(x)-\ell_\tau)/b(\tau)\) is an upper bound on \(G_\tau(x)\), not the exact gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized objective gap measures stage suboptimality; a certified lower bound yields a computable upper bound when the exact optimum is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap Diagnostics

children.title: Residual–Gap Consistency
children.top_down_role: Regimes where residual plus gap indicators provide compatible assessments.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla F_\tau(x)\|^2/(2L(\tau))\leq F_\tau(x)-F_\tau^*\leq\|\nabla F_\tau(x)\|^2/(2m(\tau))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided residual-gap comparison for smooth strongly convex stage objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(r_\tau(x):=\|\nabla F_\tau(x)\|\) and \(g_\tau(x):=F_\tau(x)-F_\tau^*\). Then \[\frac{r_\tau(x)^2}{2L(\tau)}\leq g_\tau(x)\leq\frac{r_\tau(x)^2}{2m(\tau)}.\] Therefore residual and gap tolerances are quantitatively interchangeable only when the curvature moduli are controlled. Their conversion constants differ by the condition number \(\kappa(\tau):=L(\tau)/m(\tau)\), so uniform diagnostic consistency requires uniform conditioning along the continuation path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth strongly convex stages, squared gradient residual and objective gap bound each other, with constants determined by smoothness and strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual–Gap Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-sided gradient-residual/objective-gap inequality is standard and correctly stated for smooth strongly convex objectives, but the record provides no evidence or explicit standard-field rationale for the exact bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Misleading-Diagnostic Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit diagnostic failure caused by vanishing strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_\varepsilon(x):=\varepsilon x^2/2\), the unique minimizer is \(x_\varepsilon^*=0\), while \(r_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon|x|\) and \(g_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon x^2/2\). At \(x_\varepsilon=\varepsilon^{-1/2}\), one has \(r_\varepsilon(x_\varepsilon)=\sqrt\varepsilon\to0\) but \(g_\varepsilon(x_\varepsilon)=1/2\). At \(y_\varepsilon=1\), one has \(g_\varepsilon(y_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon/2\to0\) but \(|y_\varepsilon-x_\varepsilon^*|=1\). Thus either diagnostic can mislead when curvature degenerates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing quadratic curvature makes residuals small without small gaps, and gaps small without proximity to the minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\varepsilon(x_\varepsilon)\to0\) does not imply \(g_\varepsilon(x_\varepsilon)\to0\), and \(g_\varepsilon(y_\varepsilon)\to0\) does not imply \(|y_\varepsilon-x_\varepsilon^*|\to0\), as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

children.title: Branch-Ambiguity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local path geometry permitting multiple plausible branch continuations.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\bar t]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable near \((x_*,t_*)\) and \(F(x_*,t_*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the projection \(\pi_t:S\to[0,\bar t]\), \(\pi_t(x,t)=t\), is not locally one-to-one at \((x_*,t_*)\), then the parameter value \(t_*\) does not determine a unique local continuation branch. In particular, branch ambiguity occurs when every neighborhood of \((x_*,t_*)\) contains distinct \((x_1,t),(x_2,t)\in S\) with \(x_1\ne x_2\). A sufficient local mechanism is that \(D_xF(x_*,t_*)\) is singular and two or more solution arcs through \((x_*,t_*)\) have the same parameter projection. Parameter-only continuation then requires an additional branch-selection rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\bar t]:F(x,t)=0\}\). A point \((x_*,t_*)\in S\) lies in a branch-ambiguity regime when the restriction of \(\pi_t(x,t)=t\) to \(S\) is not locally injective at that point. Equivalently, every neighborhood of \((x_*,t_*)\) contains some common parameter \(t\) and distinct solutions \(x_1\ne x_2\) satisfying \(F(x_1,t)=F(x_2,t)=0\). When multiple solution arcs meet there, the continuation parameter alone cannot identify which outgoing arc continues the incoming branch; a tangent, orientation, merit, or other branch-selection criterion is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch ambiguity occurs when arbitrarily near a continuation point, the same parameter has distinct solutions on competing local branches, so the parameter alone cannot select an outgoing path.
knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Ambiguity Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of a local path-recovery certificate based on regularity, local branch uniqueness, and convergence of a specified corrector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_*,t_*)\) satisfy \(F(x_*,t_*)=0\), with \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\bar t]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) continuously differentiable near \((x_*,t_*)\) and \(D_xF(x_*,t_*)\) nonsingular. Then there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(x_*\) and \(I\) of \(t_*\), and a unique continuously differentiable map \(x:I\to U\), such that \(x(t_*)=x_*\) and \(F(x(t),t)=0\) for every \(t\in I\). For a corrector iteration \(C_t\), define the basin of this root by \(B_t:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:C_t^j(z)\to x(t)\}\). A predictor \(p(t)\) is locally recoverable by this corrector whenever \(t\in I\) and \(p(t)\in B_t\). Loss of Jacobian nonsingularity or exit from a certified subset of \(B_t\) marks the boundary of this recovery certificate, but does not by itself prove that recovery by every method is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local recovery certificate holds where the branch is uniquely regular and the predictor belongs to the chosen corrector's basin. Losing regularity or leaving a certified part of that basin ends the certificate, not necessarily every possibility of recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\bar t]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable near \((x_*,t_*)\), and \(F(x_*,t_*)=0\).
For each relevant \(t\), \(C_t\) is the specified corrector iteration and \(p(t)\) is its predictor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist neighborhoods \(U\) and \(I\) and a unique continuously differentiable branch \(x:I\to U\). Recovery by \(C_t\) is guaranteed for predictors in \(B_t\); loss of nonsingularity or departure from a certified subset of \(B_t\) terminates this guarantee without establishing universal nonrecoverability.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Limit Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singularity of the state Jacobian at the limiting parameter of a finite-dimensional smooth continuation residual, not singular-subgradient terminology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\bar t]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable near \((x_*,0)\), with \(F(x_*,0)=0\). Suppose \(x:(0,\varepsilon]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is a differentiable solution branch satisfying \(F(x(t),t)=0\), \(x(t)\to x_*\) as \(t\downarrow0\), and \(D_xF(x(t),t)\) is nonsingular for \(t>0\). The endpoint \((x_*,0)\) is a singular limit point when \(D_xF(x_*,0)\) is singular. Continuity then gives \(\sigma_{\min}(D_xF(x(t),t))\to0\) and \(\|D_xF(x(t),t)^{-1}\|\to\infty\). On the regular portion of the branch, \(x'(t)=-D_xF(x(t),t)^{-1}D_tF(x(t),t)\). Thus the endpoint lacks a uniform state-Jacobian conditioning bound for parameter-based continuation; the tangent may become unbounded, although cancellation involving \(D_tF\) can keep it bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular limit point is an endpoint at which the limiting state Jacobian is singular. Approaching it destroys uniform inverse-Jacobian conditioning, although the path tangent need not diverge if the parameter derivative compensates.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\bar t]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable near \((x_*,0)\), and \(F(x_*,0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(D_xF(x_*,0)\) is singular, then \(\sigma_{\min}(D_xF(x(t),t))\to0\) and \(\|D_xF(x(t),t)^{-1}\|\to\infty\) as \(t\downarrow0\). Consequently, parameter-based continuation has no uniform state-Jacobian conditioning bound at the limit, though this alone does not imply that \(\|x'(t)\|\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Derivative of the residual with respect to the continuation parameter.
Differentiable solution branch approaching the limiting point.

assumptions_latex: For each parameter \(t_k\), a corrector map \(T_k\) has an attracting solution \(x_k^*\) and basin \(B_k:=\{z:T_k^j(z)\to x_k^*\}\).
The next stage is initialized by a predictor \(p_{k+1}\) computed from the current approximate solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Warm-start basin failure occurs precisely when \(p_{k+1}\notin B_{k+1}\). Local contraction estimates cannot then imply convergence to \(x_{k+1}^*\), even if the continuation branch itself remains regular. If a certified basin contains \(\{z:\|z-x_{k+1}^*\|\le r_{k+1}\}\), the checkable safe condition is \(\|p_{k+1}-x_{k+1}^*\|\le r_{k+1}\); violation marks the boundary of that certificate, though convergence outside the certified ball may still occur.

notation.meaning: Corrector iteration map at stage k.
Basin of attraction of the tracked stage solution.
Predictor used to initialize the next corrector.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(k+1\), define the basin of the desired corrected solution by \(B_{k+1}=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:T_{k+1}^j(z)\to x_{k+1}^*\}\). Warm-start basin failure is the event \(p_{k+1}\notin B_{k+1}\), where \(p_{k+1}\) is the continuation predictor. It separates geometric path existence from algorithmic tracking: the desired branch may remain regular while the corrector converges elsewhere, diverges, or stagnates. If analysis certifies a ball of radius \(r_{k+1}\) around \(x_{k+1}^*\) contained in \(B_{k+1}\), then \(\|p_{k+1}-x_{k+1}^*\|\le r_{k+1}\) is a sufficient warm-start condition; crossing that radius removes this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm-start basin failure occurs when the next predictor lies outside the attraction basin of the desired corrected solution, so branch regularity alone no longer ensures tracking.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Basin Failure

assumptions_latex: Exact stage solutions satisfy \(x_k^*=S_k(x_{k-1}^*)\), while computed stages satisfy \(x_k=S_k(x_{k-1})+d_k\).
Each stage map is Lipschitz on the relevant tracking region with constant \(q_k\ge0\), and \(\|d_k\|\le\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Writing \(e_k:=\|x_k-x_k^*\|\), one has \(e_k\le q_ke_{k-1}+\delta_k\) and therefore \[e_N\le\left(\prod_{i=1}^Nq_i\right)e_0+\sum_{j=1}^N\left(\prod_{i=j+1}^Nq_i\right)\delta_j.\] Thus stage errors remain uniformly controlled under a uniform contraction \(q_k\le q<1\) and bounded or vanishing tolerances; without contraction, nonsummable weighted errors can accumulate and destroy path tracking.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic propagation of stagewise solve errors through a finite continuation schedule.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose exact continuation stages obey \(x_k^*=S_k(x_{k-1}^*)\), whereas computed stages obey \(x_k=S_k(x_{k-1})+d_k\), with \(S_k\) Lipschitz with constant \(q_k\) and \(\|d_k\|\le\delta_k\). Then \(e_k:=\|x_k-x_k^*\|\) satisfies \(e_k\le q_ke_{k-1}+\delta_k\), and iteration gives \[e_N\le\left(\prod_{i=1}^Nq_i\right)e_0+\sum_{j=1}^N\left(\prod_{i=j+1}^Nq_i\right)\delta_j.\] The weighted sum is the cumulative inexactness. Uniform contraction attenuates old errors; absent attenuation, persistent nonsummable stage errors may prevent convergence to the limiting path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise solve errors propagate through later continuation maps as a weighted sum; contraction attenuates them, while persistent unattenuated errors can destroy limiting path accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Inexactness
